steps.do: Before you start: set CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true on the CALIBER server and restart it; MCP servers are off by default. Open the MCP Servers page and find the quick-connect catalog of 8 templates. You will use the GitHub tile because it ships both a safe read tool (search_repositories) and a risky write tool (issue_write) — perfect for proving a policy block.
steps.see: A catalog grid; the GitHub tile (test id catalog-github) sits alongside PostgreSQL, pgvector, Apache AGE, MinIO, Hugging Face, Ollama, and Playwright.

steps.do: First add api.githubcopilot.com to the CALIBER server's CALIBER_MCP_REMOTE_HOST_ALLOWLIST. Click the GitHub catalog tile. The Add-server dialog opens pre-filled with GitHub's official remote Streamable HTTP endpoint; set the server name and supply your personal-access token, then submit.
fill: your GitHub personal-access token (the env var the template expects)
steps.see: A new server row github-readonly appears in the Servers table with a Test action.

steps.do: On the server row click Test to verify the transport/auth, then let it discover the tool catalog. Inspect a couple of discovered tools and their input/output schemas so you know the read tool's required arguments.
steps.see: Connected · N tools. The discovered tool list shows search_repositories (read) and issue_write (write) with their JSON input/output schemas. Gate: connection_success_rate = 1.0.

steps.do: Open the Playground tab, select server github-readonly, click Test Connection to discover its tools, then pick the read tool search_repositories from the discovered list. Fill its parameter inputs and click Invoke Tool to confirm a real, successful result. The GitHub catalog tile pre-classifies its tools (reads allowed, writes marked write + requires approval); a tool without an explicit classification shows an Unclassified badge and its button reads “Classify Tool Before Invoking”. This is your one good read-tool invocation record.
steps.see: success:true with a result payload (mentions items) and a duration_ms figure.

steps.where: MCP Servers › Playground › issue_write › Tool Policy
steps.do: Now govern the risky write tool. Still in the Playground with github-readonly selected, pick the issue_write tool — its Tool Policy panel appears. Turn the Allow tool toggle OFF (sets allowed:false), then save. On the direct invoke path a block (allowed:false) is the only control that actually refuses execution — so use the block for a true read-only explorer. (requires_approval and side_effect_level are advisory on direct invoke; the block is what enforces.)
fill: toggle OFF → allowed:false (matches github-issue-write.block.policy.json; strip any _comment key — it is documentation only)
steps.see: The issue_write policy now shows allowed:false (a “blocked” badge appears on the tool).

steps.do: Capture the enforcement record for the now-blocked tool. In the Playground its Invoke Tool button is disabled (“Tool Blocked by Policy”) and a red Blocked badge shows, so the UI cannot send the call. Send a payload that would create an issue through the API instead (POST /mcp-servers/{id}/invoke-tool, admin scope) — it must be refused, not executed. This proves blocked_tool_enforcement = 1.0.
fill: set method=create, owner=rrahimi-uci, repo=caliber-suite, title=blocked test, body=should never be created — the PE01 row of policy-enforcement-checks.jsonl
steps.see: A structured refusal: success:false, result:null, duration_ms:0, and an error such as MCP tool 'issue_write' is blocked by policy — the tool never ran.

steps.do: Harden the read tool with a small saved suite. In the Playground with search_repositories selected, scroll to its Calibration panel. Use Add case to add a row per case; each row has a name, an Input (JSON) object (the tool arguments), and an Assertion of type no_error, output_contains, or equals (the latter two also take a value). Click Save cases. Important about the assertion model: there is no "expects-error" assertion — when an invoke errors, the case fails before any assertion runs (a gateway error short-circuits to a fail). So the two negative rows (N01 missing the required arg, N02 a malformed qualifier) are deliberately failing cases: they exist to show up as red lines in the pass-rate, not as green output_contains:"error" matches. The four golden/edge rows (G01/G02/E01/E02) are the ones expected to pass.
fill: Add the 6 cases from mcp-tool-test-cases.jsonl — four expected-pass (G01/G02 golden, E01/E02 edge) plus two intentionally-failing negatives (N01/N02). Send name + input + assertion type/value only
steps.see: Six saved test cases listed under search_repositories's Calibration panel, each showing its assertion type.

steps.do: Run the calibration. Click Run calibration in the same panel — each saved case is invoked and scored against its assertion inline (deterministic — no LLM judge), and a pass rate comes back immediately. Expect the pass-rate to land below 100% by design: the four golden/edge cases pass, and the two negative cases (N01/N02) fail because their invokes error out before any assertion can match. That red is the intended signal — it is the suite documenting how the tool misbehaves on bad input, not a defect in your setup.
steps.see: An inline pass-rate report ({pass_rate, total, passed}) — four green cases and two red negatives, so passed:4 of total:6 (a pass_rate of 0.6667, intentionally under 100%) with a per-case verdict on each row. This satisfies at_least_one_read_tool_calibrated = true.

steps.do: Confirm the evidence. The Playground History panel below the invoke form lists each invoke you ran from the Playground this session, newest first (it is in-memory browser state, lost on reload or Clear); find the search_repositories read (success:true, green dot). Click any row to reload its arguments and result. An executed invoke also emits a TOOL span named mcp.<server>.search_repositories in Observability; test-connection, discovery and the blocked refusal emit none, so the refusal lives in the API response you captured in the previous step.
steps.see: A History row with a green dot + search_repositories + a duration_ms for the successful read. The issue_write tool still wears its red Blocked badge with Invoke disabled, and the search_repositories Calibration panel still shows its saved pass/fail verdicts — together these are your end-to-end enforcement evidence.
steps.asset: playground history (read invoke) + blocked API response
